messages:
maria-support: Heads-up — customer AcmePay is hitting a sudden spike of 429s and an unexpected billing delta after yesterday's rate-limit rollout. Started ~16:12 UTC, 8x error rate for their prod token. Logs attached below.

aj-platform: Can you drop their customer_id and a sample request/response with headers? Did they migrate to the new default policy or did we enable stricter defaults?

maria-support: customer_id=acmepay-42. Sample response (scrubbed):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1670000200
content-type: application/json

{"error":"rate_exceeded","message":"You exceeded your request quota"}
```
Their client retry logic is aggressive and they normally run ~100 r/s; during spike it was 800 r/s.

tim-oncall: That x-rate-limit-* looks like the new global policy (120/s window). Was the canary push supposed to exclude high-volume customers?

aj-platform: We had a staged rollout: default limit tightened from 1000/s to 120/s for the org-level policy, but there were allowlists for reserved customers. Looks like acmepay didn't have an allowlist entry due to a missing tag in signup metadata — bug in the selector. Deploy bot shows the policy rollout id: policy-rollout-2026-03-15-2 (deployed by @deploy-bot at 2026-03-15T02:00Z).

deploy-bot: Deployment policy-rollout-2026-03-15-2 succeeded in 3 regions.

nina-cs: I just pinged AcmePay PM to apologise and told them we're triaging. They're worried about invoice spike. Any ETA on mitigation?

luca-billing: We see a usage billing jump on acmepay-42 for the same window. If they're getting 429s, why would billable tokens spike? Need meter detail — are retries being counted?

aj-platform: Retries are counted if they hit the API and consume tokens. If the client retries with backoff disabled it can create a sawtooth: they keep sending, consume tokens until 429s start, but some requests still succeed (short bursts) so net billable tokens increase. We should check the quota-meter logs: meter.v1/ingest shows per-token counts.

maria-support: Reproducer curl from their engineer:
```
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxx" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```
They acknowledged they had a bug in client backoff.

tim-oncall: Short term options: 1) rollback policy-rollout-2026-03-15-2 to previous policy, 2) add an exception (allowlist) for acmepay-42, 3) create a temporary per-token rate override. Which is least risky?

aj-platform: Rollback affects many orgs risk-wise. Best immediate mitigation is a per-customer override via the admin controlplane: POST /admin/overrides {customer_id, rate_limit: 1000, expires_in: 2h}. I can push that if someone grants approval.

nina-cs: Approve. I'll notify the customer first and confirm they'll fix client backoff.

luca-billing: Also open to doing a billing credit for the window if we confirm retries caused the spike. I'll need meter logs and request_ids.

aj-platform: Retries are counted if they hit the API and consume tokens. If the client retries with backoff disabled it can create a sawtooth: they keep sending, consume tokens until 429s start, but some requests still succeed (short bursts) so net billable tokens increase. We should check the quota-meter logs: meter.v1/ingest shows per-token counts.

maria-support: Granting access — please run the override. Here's the admin command Aj asked for:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer admin-ops-token" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://controlplane.redwood.ai/admin/v1/overrides \
  -d '{"customer_id":"acmepay-42","limit_per_second":1000,"scope":"org","expires_seconds":7200}'
```

aj-platform: Running now. Response: {"status":"ok","override_id":"ovr_9f8e7d"}. Applied in 3 regions.

deploy-bot: Override ovr_9f8e7d propagated to edge-config in 3 regions.

maria-support: Applied. Customer reports error rate dropping to baseline within ~90s.

tim-oncall: Good — keep monitoring for 30m. We should create a short rollback plan if override causes any cascading issues. Also file a ticket for the selector bug that missed acmepay tag.

aj-platform: Filed infra bug INF-1297: "policy selector ignores legacy signup tag -> customer not allowlisted." Assigning to me to fix. Plan: patch selector, run a database backfill for missing tags, then redeploy policy with a staged canary targeting 5% traffic.

nina-cs: I'll coordinate customer comms and request a short invoice hold while billing investigates.

luca-billing: I'll pull meter.v1 logs and calculate a provisional credit and follow up in a billing ticket BILL-582. Please forward request_ids for any anomalous requests.

maria-support: Attaching a small sample of request_ids we captured: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0a1b2c4e, req_0a1b2c6f.

tim-oncall: Closing temporary mitigation. Next steps: (1) aj-platform implements selector fix + backfill, (2) run canary with narrower default, (3) update rollout playbook to require explicit allowlist for historical large customers, (4) billing/CS follow-up for credit. I'll create the incident follow-up doc.

aj-platform: Acknowledged. I'll schedule the patch for tomorrow 04:00 UTC and add an explicit check to export allowlist mismatches to a queue so CS can confirm customers before rollout.

nina-cs: Thanks all — customer is satisfied for now. We'll wait on billing and the selector fix. :thumbsup:

luca-billing: Will update BILL-582 with figures by EOD.

maria-support: Marking thread resolved for triage. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
